The fix 361048f586f5 (""Btrfs: fix full backref problem when inserting
shared block reference"") added a delayed ref flushing at subvolume
creation time in order to avoid hitting this particular BUG_ON().
Before this fix
column2: we were tripping the BUG_ON() by

column1: 1. Modify snapshot A
column2: which creates blocks with a normal reference for

column1: snapshot A
column2: as A is the owner of these blocks.  We now have delayed

column1: refs for these blocks.
2. Create a snapshot of A named B
column2: which pushes references for the

column1: children blocks of the root node for the new root B
column2: thus creating

column1: more delayed refs for newly allocated blocks.
3. A is modified
column2: and because the metadata blocks can now be shared

column1: must push FULL_BACKREF references to the children of any block that A
COWs down it's path to its target key.
4. Delayed refs are run.  Because these are newly allocated blocks
column2: we

column1: have ->must_insert_reserved reserved set on the delayed ref head
column2: we

column1: call into alloc_reserved_tree_block() to add the extent item
column2: and

column1: then add our ref.  At the time of this fix
column2: we were ordering

column1: FULL_BACKREF delayed ref operations first
column2: so we'd go to add this

column1: reference and then BUG_ON() because we didn't have the FULL_BACKREF
flag set.
The patch fixed this problem by making sure we ran the delayed refs
before we had the chance to modify A.  This meant that any *new* blocks
would have had their extent items created _before_ we would ever
actually COW down and generate FULL_BACKREF entries.  Thus the problem
went away.
However this BUG_ON() is actually completely bogus.  The existence of a
full backref doesn't necessarily mean that FULL_BACKREF must be set on
that block
column2: it must only be set on the actual parent itself.  Consider

column1: the example provided above.  If we COW down one path from A
column2: any nodes

column1: are going to have a FULL_BACKREF ref pushed down to _all_ of their
children
column2: but not all of the children are going to have FULL_BACKREF

column1: set.  It is completely valid to have an extent item with normal and full
backrefs without FULL_BACKREF actually set on the block itself.
As a final note
column2: I have been testing with the patch (applied after this

column1: one)
btrfs: stop running all delayed refs during snapshot
which removed this flushing.  My test was a torture test which did a lot
of operations while snapshotting and deleting snapshots as well as
relocation
column2: and I never tripped this BUG_ON().  This is actually because

column1: at the time of 361048f586f5
column2: we ordered SHARED keys _before_ normal

column1: references
column2: and thus they would get run first.  However currently they

column1: are ordered _after_ normal references
column2: so we'd do the initial creation

column1: without having a shared reference
column2: and thus not hit this BUG_ON()

column1: explains why I didn't start hitting this problem during my testing with
my other patch applied.
